PART III  Nutrition in the Life Cycle
Bisphenol A (BPA) is a chemical that was present in many 
hard plastic bottles, such as baby bottles and reusable cups, and 
metal food and beverage containers, including canned liquid in-
fant formula. Concern has been raised about the potential effects 
of BPA on the brain, behavior, and prostate gland in fetuses, in-
fants, and young children. Since 2012, U.S. manufacturers have 
stopped producing BPA-containing bottles and infant feeding 
cups for the U.S. market. BPA has not been used in packaging for 
infant formula in the United States since 2013 (FDA, 2014).
Development of Feeding Skills

bottle but are not able to handle foods with texture. During
